slung_carriage_body.name: Slung Carriage Body
slung_carriage_body.observation: The carriage body hangs on leather straps from posts at each corner, and passengers no longer feel every stone in the road.

armed_sounding_lead.name: Armed Sounding Lead
armed_sounding_lead.observation: The leadsman fills the hollow of his lead with tallow, and the sand or shell it brings up tells the pilot where he is in fog.

two_masted_round_ships.name: Two-Masted Round Ships
two_masted_round_ships.observation: A second, smaller mast aft carries a three-cornered sail, and the round ship now holds closer to the wind.

tilt_covered_wagons.name: Tilt-Covered Wagons
tilt_covered_wagons.observation: Hooped canvas over the wagon bed keeps the carriers' cloth and grain dry through a wet week on the road.

full_rigged_three_master.name: Full-Rigged Three-Master
full_rigged_three_master.observation: Square sails on fore and main and a lateen on the mizzen let one hull run before the wind or work to windward as the voyage needs.
full_rigged_three_master.ability_reason: An admiral can keep a squadron at sea in open water through changing winds, and a merchant house can send one hull on a voyage of a year.
full_rigged_three_master.social_consequence: Shipwrights' yards grow into towns of their own, and the tallest coastal trees are marked for masts.

traverse_course_tables.name: Traverse Tables
traverse_course_tables.observation: The master reads the day's zig-zag tacks off a table and marks one line of distance made good on the chart.

lateen_caravel.name: Lateen Caravel
lateen_caravel.observation: A small lateen-rigged ship can beat home against the wind that carried it out, so captains dare to push farther along unknown coasts.

fortified_trading_posts.name: Fortified Trading Posts
fortified_trading_posts.observation: Factors of the realm live and trade behind their own walls on far coasts, with a few guns over the landing.
fortified_trading_posts.social_consequence: The factors live among strangers, and a quarrel over prices can turn a trading post into a siege.

passenger_coach.name: Passenger Coach
passenger_coach.observation: A light coach with a slung body, built in a coach-making town, carries six people and their bags at a trot.
passenger_coach.ability_reason: An official or a courier can cross the realm by coach in days instead of weeks, and people as well as letters now move between the towns.
passenger_coach.social_consequence: Travel between towns becomes ordinary for people of means, and coachmaking becomes a trade of its own.

ocean_carrack.name: Ocean Carrack
ocean_carrack.observation: A deep hold under high castles and three or four masts carries a year's cargo and a crew of a hundred across open ocean.
ocean_carrack.ability_reason: An admiral can carry an army's stores and guns across an ocean in a few deep hulls, and the high castles hold off boarders.

mariners_quadrant.name: Mariner's Quadrant
mariners_quadrant.observation: On a pitching deck the pilot sights the pole star along the quadrant's edge and reads where the plumb line falls on the scale.

topsail_rig.name: Topsails
topsail_rig.observation: Small sails set above the courses catch the wind higher up, and a ship keeps way in light airs that would have left it becalmed.

ocean_wind_circuit.name: Ocean Wind Circuit
ocean_wind_circuit.observation: Pilots stand far out to sea on the way home and find the steady winds that the coast-huggers never reach.
ocean_wind_circuit.ability_reason: An admiral can bring a fleet home from far southern coasts by standing out to sea for the prevailing winds instead of beating along the shore.

latitude_sailing.name: Latitude Sailing
latitude_sailing.observation: The pilot takes the noon sun, corrects it from his declination table, and runs down the parallel until the island rises ahead.
latitude_sailing.ability_reason: A pilot can find a far island by running down its known latitude, so a fleet commander can set a meeting place across open ocean.

ocean_victualling.name: Ocean Victualling
ocean_victualling.observation: Biscuit baked twice, beef in brine and water in hooped casks are stowed for months; the crews still sicken with bleeding gums on the long runs.

transoceanic_contact_voyages.name: Transoceanic Voyages
transoceanic_contact_voyages.observation: Ships cross the western ocean to lands no one at home had heard of, and some of them come back.
transoceanic_contact_voyages.ability_reason: An admiral can sail to the lands across the western ocean and return, so the realm can meet, trade with and settle among peoples it never knew.
transoceanic_contact_voyages.social_consequence: Sailors bring home news, seeds and sickness from peoples no one knew existed, and carry sickness to them in return.

dry_dock_services.observation: A ship is floated into a stone basin, the gates are shut and the water is pumped out, and the shipwrights walk dry-shod under its keel.

ocean_house_of_trade.name: House of Trade
ocean_house_of_trade.observation: Every ocean voyage is entered in the house of trade's books, with its cargo, crew and pilot, before the ship may sail.
ocean_house_of_trade.social_consequence: Merchants outside the chartered port complain that they are shut out of the ocean trade.

master_pattern_chart.name: Master Chart
master_pattern_chart.observation: The chief pilot corrects the master chart from each returning pilot's log, and every new chart is copied from it.

public_letter_post.name: Public Letter Post
public_letter_post.observation: The realm post now carries anyone's letters for a fee, and the postmaster-general publishes the days the riders leave.
public_letter_post.ability_reason: Merchants' letters and a general's dispatches ride the same relays on fixed days, so news from a distant army reaches the capital within days.
public_letter_post.social_consequence: Families far apart write to one another, and the postmaster's clerks learn to open and reseal letters.

examined_ocean_pilots.name: Examined Pilots
examined_ocean_pilots.observation: No pilot may take a ship across the ocean until the chief pilot has examined him on charts, stars and soundings.

buoyed_channel_corporation.name: Buoyed Channels
buoyed_channel_corporation.observation: The pilots' corporation moors buoys and keeps beacons on the harbor channel, and charges every ship that enters.

whipstaff_steering.name: Whipstaff Steering
whipstaff_steering.observation: The helmsman below deck swings a long lever to move the tiller, so even a great ship answers to one man.

gimballed_compass.name: Gimballed Compass
gimballed_compass.observation: The compass bowl hangs in two brass rings and stays level however the ship rolls.

dished_wheels.name: Dished Wheels
dished_wheels.observation: The wheels are dished outward on splayed axles, and a heavy wagon no longer racks itself to pieces in the ruts.

ocean_galleon.name: Ocean Galleon
ocean_galleon.observation: A long, low-castled hull carries both cargo and a row of guns, and sails better than the carrack it replaces.
ocean_galleon.ability_reason: An admiral gets one ocean hull that can carry cargo home and fight its way through, so treasure fleets need fewer escorts.

wagonway_haulage.observation: Trucks with flanged wheels are pushed along timber rails from the pit to the staithe, and one man moves what took four carriers.

escorted_ocean_fleets.name: Escorted Ocean Fleets
escorted_ocean_fleets.observation: The merchant ships wait for the fleet and sail together twice a year under warships, and come home with bullion and goods.
escorted_ocean_fleets.ability_reason: An admiral can shepherd a whole year's ocean trade in one guarded convoy, and raiders must now fight warships to take a prize.
escorted_ocean_fleets.social_consequence: The ports empty and fill twice a year, and prices swing wildly between the fleets.

cross_ocean_galleon_run.name: Galleon Run
cross_ocean_galleon_run.observation: One great galleon a year crosses the widest ocean, carrying silver out and silk and porcelain back.
cross_ocean_galleon_run.social_consequence: Silver pours out and silk pours in, and prices in the ports rise year after year.

straight_course_projection_charts.name: Straight-Course Charts
straight_course_projection_charts.observation: The new chart stretches the lands toward the poles so that a compass course is a straight line drawn with a ruler.
straight_course_projection_charts.ability_reason: A fleet's pilot can lay one straight compass course across an ocean chart and hold it, so squadrons can be sent to distant stations with confidence.

log_and_line.name: Log and Line
log_and_line.observation: A board on a knotted line is thrown astern, and the knots that run out while the sandglass empties give the ship's speed.

printed_sea_atlases.name: Printed Sea Atlases
printed_sea_atlases.observation: Charts and sailing directions for a whole coast are printed and bound together, and any master can buy them.

backstaff.name: Backstaff
backstaff.observation: The navigator stands with his back to the sun and lines up its shadow, and no longer ruins his eyes to take the noon height.

fluyt_bulk_carrier.name: Bulk Carrier
fluyt_bulk_carrier.observation: A cheap, narrow-decked hull with simple rigging carries grain and timber with half the crew of older ships.
fluyt_bulk_carrier.ability_reason: Grain, timber and an army's bulk supplies can go by sea at half the old freight, with small crews.
fluyt_bulk_carrier.social_consequence: Rival ports lose their carrying trade to the cheap hulls, and old crews are paid off.

company_merchant_fleets.name: Company Fleets
company_merchant_fleets.observation: Chartered companies send their own fleets, keep factors and warehouses abroad and pay dividends to shareholders at home.
company_merchant_fleets.social_consequence: The companies keep their own soldiers abroad and answer to their shareholders more than to the realm.

entrepot_reexport_port.name: Entrepot Port
entrepot_reexport_port.observation: Far-sea goods are landed, stored and shipped on again to every port along the coast.

endorsed_bills.name: Endorsed Bills
endorsed_bills.observation: A merchant signs the back of a bill of exchange and pays his own debt with it, and the bill passes through a dozen hands before it is paid.

ship_logbooks.name: Ship Logbooks
ship_logbooks.observation: Course, speed, wind and weather are written in the ship's log every watch, and the owners read it when the ship comes home.

azimuth_variation_finding.name: Compass Variation
azimuth_variation_finding.observation: The navigator takes the sun's bearing as it rises, and the difference from true east tells him how far his compass points wrong here.

hackney_coaches.name: Hackney Coaches
hackney_coaches.observation: Coaches stand for hire in the town streets, and anyone with the fare can ride across the city.

navigators_log_scale.name: Navigator's Scale
navigators_log_scale.observation: A ruled scale of logarithms lets the navigator work a course with a pair of dividers instead of long sums.

victualling_yards.name: Victualling Yards
victualling_yards.observation: State yards bake biscuit, salt beef and brew beer by the shipload, and every cask is marked with its yard and year.

scheduled_passenger_barges.name: Passenger Barges
scheduled_passenger_barges.observation: Horse-drawn barges leave the town quay at fixed hours, and passengers sleep or read on the way.

carriers_guide.name: Carriers' Guide
carriers_guide.observation: A printed guide lists every carrier, the inn he leaves from and the days he goes, for every town in the realm.

distance_postage_rates.name: Distance Postage
distance_postage_rates.observation: The post office prints its rates by distance, and a letter costs the same to send whoever sends it.

staircase_summit_canal.name: Summit Canal
staircase_summit_canal.observation: Flights of locks lift barges over the watershed, and a reservoir on the summit feeds the locks through the dry season.
staircase_summit_canal.ability_reason: Barges can cross the watershed between two river basins, so grain, timber and an army's stores move by water across the width of the realm.

scheduled_stage_wagons.name: Stage Wagons
scheduled_stage_wagons.observation: Great wagons leave on fixed days between the towns, and carriers sell space by the hundredweight.

own_hull_navigation_law.name: Navigation Law
own_hull_navigation_law.observation: The realm's cargoes may be carried only in the realm's own ships, crewed mostly by its own seamen.
own_hull_navigation_law.social_consequence: Foreign carriers are shut out, freight costs rise, and the realm's shipyards and seamen multiply.

long_route_stagecoaches.name: Long-Route Stagecoaches
long_route_stagecoaches.observation: Stagecoaches run the long roads on a published timetable and change teams at an inn every stage.
long_route_stagecoaches.ability_reason: Officials, officers and couriers can cross the realm on a published schedule, so orders and reports reach a distant army in a fraction of the old time.

river_navigation_commissions.name: River Commissions
river_navigation_commissions.observation: Commissioners dredge the shoals, cut through the loops and build towpaths, and charge tolls on every barge.

steel_leaf_springs.name: Leaf Springs
steel_leaf_springs.observation: Stacked leaves of springy steel carry the coach body, and the ride is steadier at speed.

broad_wheel_laws.name: Broad-Wheel Laws
broad_wheel_laws.observation: Heavy wagons must run on wheels a hand's breadth wide, which roll the road flat instead of cutting it.

printed_road_books.name: Printed Road Books
printed_road_books.observation: Strip maps show each road in measured miles, with every inn, bridge and turning marked.

two_sea_canal.name: Two-Sea Canal
two_sea_canal.observation: A canal climbs over the land between two seas, and barges carry the through trade without the long voyage around the coast.
two_sea_canal.ability_reason: Barges and a fleet's stores can pass between two seas inland, avoiding a long and dangerous voyage around the coast.

mail_packet_ships.name: Mail Packets
mail_packet_ships.observation: Fast small ships carry the mail across the sea on fixed sailing days, with or without a full cargo.

underwriters_room.name: Underwriters' Room
underwriters_room.observation: Underwriters meet in a coffee house, read the ship news together and each sign for a share of the risk.
underwriters_room.social_consequence: A loss at sea ruins a syndicate rather than a single house, and shipowners take bolder risks.

jib_staysail_rig.name: Jibs and Staysails
jib_staysail_rig.observation: Triangular sails set on the stays between the masts help the ship go about quickly and point higher.

builders_measure_tonnage.name: Builder's Measure
builders_measure_tonnage.observation: A ship's tonnage is worked from its length and beam by a fixed rule, and its dues are charged on that.

crossroad_fingerposts.name: Fingerposts
crossroad_fingerposts.observation: The parish must set up a post at every crossroads with arms pointing to the next towns and their distances.

draft_horse_breeding.name: Draft Horse Breeding
draft_horse_breeding.observation: Breeders select heavy horses for the freight wagons, and a team of six now pulls what eight could before.

ships_steering_wheel.name: Ship's Wheel
ships_steering_wheel.observation: A wheel on deck works the tiller through ropes and blocks, and the helmsman can see the sails as he steers.

coasting_schooner.name: Coasting Schooner
coasting_schooner.observation: A fore-and-aft rigged schooner works along the coast with a handful of men and slips into small harbors.

bonded_warehouses.name: Bonded Warehouses
bonded_warehouses.observation: Goods in transit sit under the customs lock without paying duty until they are taken out for sale at home.

printed_cargo_forms.name: Printed Cargo Forms
printed_cargo_forms.observation: The manifest, the bill of lading and the charter are printed forms, and a clerk fills in the blanks.

drawn_hull_plans.name: Drawn Hull Plans
drawn_hull_plans.observation: The shipwright draws the body plan and carves a half-model before any timber is cut, and sister ships come out alike.

post_chaise_hire.name: Post Chaises
post_chaise_hire.observation: A light chaise and fresh horses are hired at every posting inn, and a traveller in a hurry covers a hundred miles a day.

reflecting_octant.name: Reflecting Octant
reflecting_octant.observation: Two mirrors bring the sun down to the horizon in one view, so the angle can be read even on a rolling deck.
reflecting_octant.ability_reason: An admiral's position at sea is known to a few miles rather than to a day's sail, so fleets are lost on unknown shoals far less often.

printed_shipping_lists.name: Shipping Lists
printed_shipping_lists.observation: A printed list of every ship arrived, sailed or lost is sold twice a week at the exchange.

turnpike_milestones.name: Turnpike Milestones
turnpike_milestones.observation: A stone every mile along the turnpike gives the distance to the next towns, and the coaches keep time by them.

night_fly_wagons.name: Night Fly Wagons
night_fly_wagons.observation: Fast wagons change horses and drivers and run through the night, and goods reach the capital in half the time.

coastal_hydrographic_survey.name: Coastal Survey
coastal_hydrographic_survey.observation: Survey parties fix the headlands by triangles from the shore and sound the bays from boats.

sextant.name: Sextant
sextant.observation: The larger arc of the sextant measures the wide angle between the moon and a star.
sextant.ability_reason: Navigators can measure the wide angles that lunar tables need, so a fleet can fix its longitude as well as its latitude.

lunar_distance_longitude.name: Lunar Longitude
lunar_distance_longitude.observation: The navigator measures the moon's distance from a star, works the sum from the printed tables, and knows how far east or west he is.
lunar_distance_longitude.ability_reason: An admiral can fix his position east and west by the moon, so squadrons meet at rendezvous in open ocean and far coasts are no longer found by luck.

contour_coal_canal.name: Contour Coal Canal
contour_coal_canal.observation: A canal winds level along the hillside from the pit mouth to the city, and a barge of coal costs half what the carts charged.
contour_coal_canal.ability_reason: Coal and heavy goods move by barge at half the cart price, so a town's fuel and an arsenal's iron no longer wait on the roads.

nautical_almanac.name: Nautical Almanac
nautical_almanac.observation: Each year a printed almanac gives the lunar distances worked out ahead, and the navigator no longer needs to be an astronomer.

iron_plated_wagonway_rails.name: Iron-Plated Rails
iron_plated_wagonway_rails.observation: Iron plates nailed along the timber rails carry heavier trucks and wear for years.

marine_timekeeper.name: Marine Timekeeper
marine_timekeeper.observation: A clock that keeps the home port's time through heat, cold and rolling gives the longitude by comparison with local noon.
marine_timekeeper.ability_reason: A navigator knows his longitude from the clock at any noon, so an admiral can station ships and find islands without waiting for the moon.

copper_hull_sheathing.name: Copper Sheathing
copper_hull_sheathing.observation: Thin copper plates nailed over the hull keep out shipworm and weed, and a ship stays fast for years between refits.

canal_share_companies.name: Canal Companies
canal_share_companies.observation: A canal company sells shares, buys the land under its charter and charges tolls on every barge.
canal_share_companies.social_consequence: Landowners and merchants buy canal shares, and a rush for them ruins some of the buyers.

trunk_canal_cross.name: Trunk Canal Cross
trunk_canal_cross.observation: Trunk canals join four river systems, and a barge can cross the realm from any of its ports to any other.

timed_mail_coaches.name: Timed Mail Coaches
timed_mail_coaches.observation: Mail coaches with an armed guard run to a timetable through the night, and the guard's watch is set and checked at each stage.
timed_mail_coaches.ability_reason: Dispatches to a distant army arrive on a day that can be counted on, and valuables travel with a guard between the cities.

hydrographic_office.name: Hydrographic Office
hydrographic_office.observation: A state office collects the surveys, engraves the charts and sells them to any master.

trial_steam_paddle_boat.name: Trial Paddle Boat
trial_steam_paddle_boat.observation: A boiler and engine turn paddle wheels, and the boat creeps upstream against the current until something breaks.
